description: 12 test prompts for Ornith-1.0-9B IQ3_M evaluation on Jetson Orin Nano 8GB — adapted from jetson-model-zoo

prompts.name: HTML Profile Cards Page
prompts.prompt: Create a complete HTML page with CSS that displays 3 profile cards side by side. Each card should have a circular avatar placeholder, a name, a job title, and a short bio. Use flexbox for layout. Include hover effects on the cards. Make it responsive so cards stack vertically on mobile. Return only the HTML file.

scoring_rubric.10: Complete, responsive, hover effects, clean CSS, valid HTML, visually appealing
scoring_rubric.7-8: Complete HTML with most features, minor CSS issues
scoring_rubric.5-6: Basic HTML, missing responsiveness or hover, functional but rough
scoring_rubric.3-4: Incomplete or broken layout, missing major features

prompts.name: HTML Web Browser Game
prompts.prompt: Create a single HTML file with JavaScript for a simple click-the-target game. A colored circle appears at random positions on a canvas. The player clicks it to score points. Show the score, a 30-second timer, and a game over screen with final score. Include a start button. Return only the HTML file.

scoring_rubric.10: Working game with all features: random targets, scoring, timer, game over, start button
scoring_rubric.5-6: Partial game, missing timer or score tracking
scoring_rubric.1-2: Not a game or completely wrong

prompts.name: Python Data Processing
prompts.prompt: Write a Python function called process_grades that takes a list of dictionaries, where each dict has 'name' and 'score' keys. The function should: 1) Calculate the average score, 2) Find the highest and lowest scorers, 3) Return a summary dict with avg_score, top_student, and bottom_student. Include type hints and a docstring. Include a test example.

scoring_rubric.10: Correct logic, type hints, docstring, test example, handles edge cases, clean code
scoring_rubric.7-8: Correct logic, missing type hints or docstring or edge case handling
scoring_rubric.5-6: Works for basic case, minor logic errors or missing test

prompts.name: Iambic Pentameter Poem
prompts.prompt: Write a 6-line poem in strict iambic pentameter about a lighthouse keeper watching a storm. Each line must have exactly 10 syllables with the da-DUM da-DUM da-DUM da-DUM da-DUM rhythm. Do not add extra commentary. Return only the poem.

scoring_rubric.10: Exactly 6 lines, perfect iambic pentameter (10 syllables, correct stress), evocative imagery
scoring_rubric.7-8: 6 lines, mostly correct meter, 1-2 syllable count errors
scoring_rubric.5-6: 6 lines but meter is inconsistent, or wrong syllable count on multiple lines
scoring_rubric.3-4: Wrong line count, mostly wrong meter
scoring_rubric.1-2: Not a poem or completely ignores meter requirement

prompts.name: Mathematical Proof
prompts.prompt: Prove that the sum of the first n natural numbers equals n(n+1)/2. Use mathematical induction. Show the base case, the inductive hypothesis, and the inductive step clearly. Return only the proof.

scoring_rubric.10: Correct base case, correct inductive hypothesis, correct inductive step, clear notation
scoring_rubric.7-8: Correct proof, minor notation or clarity issues
scoring_rubric.5-6: Mostly correct, one step unclear or slightly wrong
scoring_rubric.1-2: Not a proof or completely wrong

prompts.name: Creative Writing - Short Story
prompts.prompt: Write a 200-word short story about a musician who discovers their old guitar can play memories. The story should have a clear beginning, middle, and end. Use vivid sensory details. Return only the story.

scoring_rubric.10: Compelling narrative arc, vivid sensory details, ~200 words, creative premise well-executed
scoring_rubric.7-8: Good story, slightly over/under word count, decent sensory detail
scoring_rubric.5-6: Basic story, weak narrative arc, far from word count
scoring_rubric.3-4: Barely a story, no narrative structure
scoring_rubric.1-2: Not a story or completely off-topic

prompts.name: Function Call: Web Search
prompts.prompt: I need to find recent news about renewable energy breakthroughs. Search the web for the latest developments in solar and wind technology from this month.

scoring_rubric.10: Calls web_search with a well-formed query about renewable energy breakthroughs
scoring_rubric.7-8: Attempts web_search but query could be better
scoring_rubric.5-6: Mentions searching but doesn't properly call the tool
scoring_rubric.3-4: Answers from training data, doesn't attempt tool use

prompts.name: Function Call: Terminal Command
prompts.prompt: Check the disk usage on my system and tell me how much free space is left on the root partition.

scoring_rubric.10: Calls terminal with 'df -h' or equivalent to check disk usage
scoring_rubric.7-8: Attempts terminal command but slightly wrong syntax
scoring_rubric.5-6: Mentions checking disk but doesn't call terminal
scoring_rubric.3-4: Gives generic answer without running anything

prompts.name: Function Call: Write File
prompts.prompt: Create a file called todo.txt in my home directory with these items: 1. Buy groceries 2. Call dentist 3. Fix the sink. Save it to ~/todo.txt.

scoring_rubric.10: Calls write_file with correct path and all 3 todo items
scoring_rubric.7-8: Attempts write_file but path or content slightly off
scoring_rubric.5-6: Mentions creating file but doesn't call write_file

prompts.name: Function Call: Read File
prompts.prompt: Read the contents of /etc/hostname and tell me what it says.

scoring_rubric.7-8: Attempts to read but wrong tool or path
scoring_rubric.5-6: Mentions reading but doesn't call a tool

prompts.name: Function Call: SQLite Query
prompts.prompt: Query the database at clinic.db for all patients seen in the last 30 days. Show me their names and visit dates.

scoring_rubric.10: Constructs and runs a proper SQLite query with date filtering
scoring_rubric.7-8: Attempts SQLite query but syntax or date logic slightly off
scoring_rubric.5-6: Mentions SQL but doesn't execute it

prompts.name: Function Call: Email Draft
prompts.prompt: Draft an email to my colleague Sarah about rescheduling our Thursday meeting to Monday at 2pm. The email should be professional and brief.

scoring_rubric.10: Well-structured email with subject line, greeting, body, sign-off. Professional tone, brief, clear about reschedule
scoring_rubric.7-8: Good email, missing subject line or slightly verbose
scoring_rubric.5-6: Basic email, missing structure or tone issues
scoring_rubric.1-2: Not an email or completely off-topic
